title: Watson — From Japanese Corporate Enclave to Multicultural Working-Class District
content: Originally built over the northern ruins for Arasaka executives and top-tier corporate clinics, Watson lost its backing after the crash of '23 and now blends Asian immigrant communities, crowded bazaars, and working-class industrial blocks. Throughout Act 1, the NCPD keeps its bridges locked down until after The Heist at Konpeki Plaza.

title: Little China — Megabuilding H10, Viktor's Clinic, and Tom's Diner
content: The dense, neon-drenched vertical heart of Watson beside the canals. Here rises Megabuilding H10—home to V's starting apartment, Wilson's gun shop, and the back lot where we first met—alongside Viktor Vektor's back-alley clinic, Misty's Esoterica, and Tom's Diner. Patrolled heavily by the NCPD, with Tyger Claws and Scavenger crews lurking in the back alleys.

title: Kabuki — Black-Market Cyberware Bazaar and Lizzie's Bar
content: A vertical labyrinth of covered walkways, tangled pipes, and cramped stalls wedged between Watson and Japantown. By day, secondhand cyberware markets and back-alley clinics bustle with business; by night, The Mox hold down Lizzie's Bar while Tyger Claws crews and Scavenger cells lurk in the basements.

title: Northside (NID) — All Foods Plant, Docks, and Totentanz
content: Watson's grimiest industrial belt: wedged among Petrochem refineries, abandoned synthetic-meat plants like All Foods, and volatile CHOOH2 storage tanks, Maelstrom rules the turf around the industrial metal club Totentanz perched atop a crumbling ruin.

title: Arasaka Waterfront — Watson's Walled Corporate Port
content: A heavily fortified port zone along Watson's western shoreline, sealed behind concrete walls, automated turrets, and relentless Arasaka patrols. Key corporate freighters dock here—like the Ebunike tied to Adam Smasher and Grayson—alongside military warehouses linked to the Dashi Parade.

title: Afterlife — Little China's Sanctuary for Mercs and Legends
content: Built inside a converted underground morgue in Watson and run by Rogue Amendiares, the Afterlife is the epicenter of Night City's mercenary elite. Every booth holds confidential fixer deals while Claire pours signature cocktails named after edgerunners who went out in a blaze of glory.

title: Westbrook — Luxury, Nightlife, and Neokitsch Power
content: Partially leveled during the 2023 catastrophe and rebuilt by wealthy corpos in the 2040s and 2050s, Westbrook blends Japantown's neon entertainment towers, Charter Hill's upscale apartments, and North Oak's fortified hillside mansions.

title: Japantown — Jig-Jig Street, Clouds, and the Cherry Blossom Market
content: Night City's biggest after-hours showcase: streets packed with Japanese holograms, the terraced Cherry Blossom Market shrine, the seedy Jig-Jig Street alley of cut-rate ripperdocs and black-market braindances, Wakako's parlor, and the doll suites of Clouds inside Megabuilding H8.

title: Charter Hill — Corporate Exec Residences and Lele Park
content: A terraced subdistrict bridging North Oak's wealth and Japantown's neon glare, where mid-level corporate managers, Biotechnica specialists, and lawyers live behind gated checkpoints, surveillance cameras, and private security drones—all quietly watched by Wakako.

title: North Oak — Fortified Hills, Mansions, and the Columbarium
content: Exclusive northeastern hills high enough that even the smog thins out: armored villas belonging to rockstars like Kerry Eurodyne, Arasaka family estates complete with artificial forests, and the monumental Columbarium cemetery lined with niches bearing legendary names.

title: Corpo Plaza — Monolithic Skyscrapers Over 2023 Ground Zero
content: Raised after clearing the radioactive rubble left by the 2023 nuke, Corpo Plaza is a colossal traffic ring flanked by the glass headquarters of Arasaka, Militech, Petrochem, Kang Tao, and Biotechnica surrounding Memorial Park.

title: Downtown — Financial District, Dino Dinovic, and Konpeki Plaza
content: The corporate and financial waterfront west of Corpo Plaza, ruled by fixer Dino Dinovic's network, upscale nightclubs, the exclusive Embers restaurant, and Arasaka's artificial peninsula crowned by the luxury fortress hotel Konpeki Plaza.

title: Heywood: The Glen & Wellsprings — City Hall, High-Rises, and Sharp Contrasts
content: Heywood's sleeker, landscaped northern side houses City Hall, green spaces like Reconciliation Park, and upscale residential towers around The Glen and Wellsprings—forming a sharp border between downtown corporate wealth and the struggling barrios.

title: Vista del Rey — El Coyote Cojo, Delamain HQ, and Valentino Turf
content: Heywood's gritty working-class heart, wedged between elevated highways and weathered apartment blocks where the Valentinos guard their streets. It holds Delamain's automated headquarters, Padre Ibarra's parish, and Mama Welles's iconic neighborhood bar, El Coyote Cojo.

title: Santo Domingo & Arroyo — Power Plant, Dam, and Heavy Industry
content: Arroyo packs the mega power plants, chemical pipelines, industrial scrapyards, and assembly factories that keep Night City running—circling the dried-out dam and warehouses patrolled by 6th Street under fixer Muamar 'El Capitan' Reyes's network.

title: Rancho Coronado — Factory Suburb, Megabuilding H4, and Edgerunners Turf
content: A geometric sprawl of identical prefab tract homes beside Megabuilding H4 where factory workers scrape by in Santo Domingo. These streets and rooftops raised David Martinez before the fateful year of 2076, under the close watch of 6th Street patrols.

title: Pacifica (Coastview & West Wind) — The Pacific Combat Zone
content: Pitched in the sixties as a seaside resort paradise and abandoned mid-construction when the Unification War scared off investors, Pacifica has zero NCPD coverage: crumbling hotels framed by a rusted Ferris wheel skeleton, the Grand Imperial Mall held by the Animals, and Voodoo Boys turf in Coastview.

title: Dogtown (Phantom Liberty) — Petrochem Stadium, Black Sapphire, and Heavy Hearts
content: A walled citadel inside Pacifica ruled de facto by Kurt Hansen and BARGHEST since 2070. Its underground economy runs on the black market inside the massive EBM Petrochem Stadium, the ultra-luxurious Black Sapphire tower, Mr. Hands's Heavy Hearts pyramid club, and looted airdrops.

title: The Badlands — Desert, Rocky Ridge, Sunset Motel, and Biotechnica Flats
content: Arid expanses ringing Night City amid crimson sandstorms, burning oil fields, the ghost town of Rocky Ridge, and the Sunset Motel. To the east and south rise Nomad comm towers and endless miles of turret-guarded Biotechnica greenhouses.

title: Laguna Bend — The Sunken Town Beneath the Toxic Reservoir
content: A once-quiet town southeast of Night City deliberately flooded by an energy corp to create an artificial reservoir. Its houses, school, and church sit intact beneath contaminated waters—and it's where Judy Alvarez grew up with her grandfather before moving to the city.
